cards.note: Matthew 12:38 — *Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from thee.* *In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.* (Matthew 28:1) The scribes and Pharisees asked for a sign, and Yahusha (Jesus) told them they would be given only one, Jonah's: *so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth* (Matthew 12:40). The two Marys going to look at the sepulchre as the first day of the week begins to dawn are standing where that sign comes due.

cards.note: Matthew 26:32 — *But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.* *In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.* (Matthew 28:1) On the Mount of Olives Yahusha (Jesus) had already told his disciples, who were about to be scattered, where he would meet them once he was raised. The angel's word to the women, *he goeth before you into Galilee* (Matthew 28:7), is that same promise being kept, so the empty tomb breaks nothing he had not said.

cards.note: Leviticus 23:15 — *And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete:* *In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.* (Matthew 28:1) Leviticus starts the counting *from the morrow after the sabbath*, the day after the sheaf of the wave offering is brought, and Matthew sets the women at the sepulchre as one sabbath ends and the first day of the week dawns. That puts the empty tomb on a morning after a sabbath, the morning the firstfruits count begins.

members.member_note: *Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption* (Tehillim/Psalm 16:10).
*Yoseph (Joseph) of Arimathaea craving the body — the burial in the rich man's tomb that fulfills Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 53:9.* *He made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death.*
*He is risen; he is not here.* Tehillim (Psalm) 16:10's *thou wilt not leave my soul in hell* carries the resurrection-substance.
Tehillim (Psalm) 22:22-24's *in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee* — the post-resurrection vindication-arc.
*Thou wilt not leave my soul in sheol.*
The substantial-vindication-substance — *I will declare thy name unto my brethren*.
*In the third day he will raise us up.*
*Declared to be the Son of Elohim with power ... by the resurrection from the dead.*

Matthew 12:38 — *Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from thee.* The scribes and Pharisees ask for a sign, and the only one Yahusha (Jesus) gives them is Jonah's, the one the sepulchre answers.

Matthew 26:32 — *But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.* Before his arrest Yahusha (Jesus) says he will go before his disciples into Galilee after he is raised, and the angel at the tomb repeats it.

Leviticus 23:15 — *from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering.* The count to the feast of weeks starts the morrow after the sabbath, the same kind of morning on which the women find the tomb empty.

threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. The women come to the tomb at the end of the Sabbath and are told what he had told them:

*In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.* (Matthew 28:1)

*He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6)

*But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.* (Matthew 26:32)

David had written the rising a thousand years before, and Peter and Paul both said this was the verse:

*For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.* (Psalm 16:10)

*He seeing this before spake of the resurrection of Messiah (Christ), that his soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption.* (Acts 2:31)

*Wherefore he saith also in another psalm, Thou shalt not suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.* (Acts 13:35)

The third day was Hosea's, spoken over the house that would be raised up, and Jonah's, which Yahusha (Jesus) took as his own sign:

*After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight.* (Hosea 6:2)

*Now Yahuah (LORD) had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.* (Jonah 1:17)

*For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.* (Matthew 12:40)

And the morning itself was in the Torah's calendar. The sheaf of firstfruits is waved before Yahuah (the LORD) on the morrow after the Sabbath, in Passover week, and Paul calls the risen one by the sheaf's name:

*Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, When ye be come into the land which I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest:* (Leviticus 23:10)

*And he shall wave the sheaf before Yahuah (LORD), to be accepted for you: on the morrow after the sabbath the priest shall wave it.* (Leviticus 23:11)

*But now is Messiah (Christ) risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.* (1 Corinthians 15:20)

*But every man in his own order: Messiah (Christ) the firstfruits; afterward they that are Messiah's (Christ’s) at his coming.* (1 Corinthians 15:23)

A firstfruits sheaf is the first of a harvest, waved so that the rest may be accepted. He rose on the day the sheaf was waved, first of them that slept, and the order Paul gives is the order of the harvest: he first, afterward those that are his at his coming. The rising is also the Father's word over the trial's verdict:

*And declared to be the Son of Elohim (God) with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:* (Romans 1:4)

The council said blasphemy. The empty tomb on the morning of the sheaf said Son of Elohim (God), with power.
